issues.body:
`select(.conclusion != "action_required")` treats every `action_required` run as ingestion-rejection evidence. This repo's own detector says that is not sound. scripts/ci-latency-alert.py:307-311: "a scheduled run held by an ENVIRONMENT protection rule can also conclude `action_required` — and this repo does gate privileged jobs on the `dispatch-secrets` environment. That run HAS jobs. Zero jobs is what separates 'GitHub refused to ingest the file' from 'a human has not approved a deployment', so the count is confirmed before alarming."

Every run-anchored target of this leg is in exactly that population: metrics.yml:40,172, conflict-resolver.yml:28, curate.yml:23, groom-core.yml:30 all carry `environment: dispatch-secrets`, as does dashboard.yml:151,349,444 (the metrics.yml leg's target).

Failure sequence: a scheduled run is held for `dispatch-secrets` approval and SETTLES (denied or timed out) with conclusion `action_required`, status `completed`. The #559 live-run guard keys on `.status != "completed"`, so it cannot see a settled run. The anchor filter discards it. `last` is empty, `prev=0`, `age` is the full Unix epoch, and the workflow is dispatched — producing another approval-gated run that settles the same way. The leg then kicks that workflow on every */15 fire indefinitely, while emitting a false ingestion-rejection annotation: the #559 dup-dispatch storm through a door the guard cannot cover.

The step comment names the divergence ("this recovery loop does not query jobs to distinguish settled approval-gated runs") but stops at naming it. The consequence is neither analysed nor bounded, and no self-test drives it — the new fixtures only ever supply `action_required` runs meant as rejections, never as approval holds, so the suite stays green through the whole scenario.

Same defect in .github/workflows/metrics.yml:298 and in dashboard.yml's cross-repo leg.
issues.fix_hint: Either (a) reuse M4's discriminator — for a run whose conclusion is `action_required`, read `actions/runs/<id>/jobs?per_page=1` and only exclude it from the anchor when `total_count == 0`, treating an unreadable count as NOT-excluded (fail toward liveness, matching fetch_job_count's None-is-not-zero rule at ci-latency-alert.py:1210-1224); or (b) if the extra request per rejected-looking run is unacceptable in this leg, do not change the kick decision at all — keep the pre-PR anchor and let the new `::error::` annotation be the only new behaviour, leaving human recovery to M4 as the comment already says it does. Whichever is chosen, add a self-test row supplying a settled `action_required` run WITH jobs and assert the target is not kicked.
issues.title: action_required is excluded without the job-count discriminator, so an approval-gated run becomes a permanent 15-minute kick loop on every watched workflow

issues.body:
Before this change, a pure rejected stream read as fresh and the loop moved on. Now `last` is empty, `age` is the full epoch, and the leg always reaches `gh api -X POST .../dispatches`. That call is not wrapped in `|| true`, and the step runs under `set -euo pipefail`.

In precisely the state this PR targets — GitHub refusing to ingest the workflow file — the dispatch POST is the request most likely to fail (a workflow whose file cannot be read has no readable `workflow_dispatch` trigger; the API answers 422). A non-zero `gh` exit there terminates the step, so every remaining spec in `for spec in metrics.yml:1200 conflict-resolver.yml:1500 curate.yml:2400 dispatch.yml:1200:dispatch-tick groom-core.yml:1800 retriage.yml:3600` is never evaluated. metrics.yml is FIRST, so a single rejected metrics.yml converts a targeted non-curative kick into a mesh-wide keepalive outage for conflict-resolver, curate, dispatch, groom-core and retriage — the exact opposite of the fail-open discipline every other read in this step observes (`|| true`, `|| echo ""`, and the #922/#559 FAIL-OPEN rows that assert it).

The self-test cannot see this: the stub's `*/dispatches) exit 0` case makes the dispatch infallible, so both new `(0, ["metrics.yml"])` rows pass regardless. The comment added at dashboard.yml ("a kick is knowingly non-curative; the error annotation is the payload") accepts the wasted kick but does not consider that the kick can take the rest of the loop down with it.

Same shape in .github/workflows/metrics.yml:298 (single-spec loop, so the blast radius there is the step's own exit status rather than sibling specs).
issues.fix_hint: Make the kick non-fatal to the loop: `gh api -X POST ".../dispatches" -f ref=master || echo "::error::keepalive: ${wf} dispatch failed — target may be un-ingestable"`. Add a `dispatch_fail` fixture to the stub (an env-gated non-zero exit on the `*/dispatches` branch) and a row asserting that when the FIRST spec's dispatch fails the later specs are still evaluated and the stale one among them is still kicked — otherwise the fail-open property is asserted for the two reads and left uncovered for the write.
issues.title: An empty anchor now guarantees a dispatch, and the unguarded POST under `set -e` lets one rejected workflow wedge the whole keepalive loop

issues.body:
`if [ -z "$last" ]` is reached by three distinct states, and the message names only one of them:

1. The API read FAILED. The command ends in `|| true` precisely so a blip does not wedge the leg, so a transient 5xx or a rate-limit yields `last=""`. The leg then prints `has no accepted run among its newest 30; action_required runs are not liveness evidence` — a confident, specific, and false diagnosis of a network error.
2. The workflow has never run (newly added file, or a disabled workflow whose runs are not listed — ci-latency-alert.py:329-331 is explicit that "disabled" is a distinct state from "unhealthy").
3. All 30 newest runs really are `action_required` — the only case the message describes.

In a repo whose stated posture is that annotations are the payload and that indeterminate must never collapse into a finding (see M4_INDETERMINATE_STATES and the None-is-not-zero rule at ci-latency-alert.py:1213-1214), emitting a definite cause for an indeterminate read is the same class of error M4 was built to avoid.

Coverage gap alongside it: the harness has `artifacts_fail` and `live_fail` fixtures only, and this diff narrows `STUB_LIVE_FAIL` to the branch matching `status != "completed"` — correctly, for the #559 rows — which leaves the newly reshaped anchor read with no way to be made to fail at all. So state 1 above, the one the leg tolerates by design and now mislabels, is executed by nothing.

Identical text in .github/workflows/dashboard.yml (both legs).
issues.fix_hint: Distinguish the read failure from the empty result at the call site, e.g. capture status separately (`if ! last=$(gh api ... --jq '...'); then echo "::warning::keepalive: ${wf} run listing unreadable — falling through to the age check"; last=""; elif [ -z "$last" ]; then echo "::error::keepalive: ${wf} has no accepted run among its newest 30"; fi`), and drop the causal claim from the message or qualify it. Add a `runs_fail` fixture to run_keepalive_leg (STUB_RUNS_FAIL on the `action_required` branch) with a row asserting the anchor read still fails open AND that the annotation emitted is the unreadable-listing one, not the no-accepted-run one.
issues.title: The `::error::` annotation asserts one cause for three conditions, and the anchor read's fail-open path is untestable in the harness

issues.body:
`run_keepalive_leg` now injects `METRICS_RESULT="failure"` unconditionally into the environment of every leg it drives. The value is necessary — the metrics step body reads `${METRICS_RESULT}` under `set -u`, so without it the newly added metrics-leg rows would abort rather than run — but hardcoding it in the shared helper means the OTHER branch of that step can never be reached by this harness.

That branch is not incidental. Its own comment (metrics.yml:275-284) documents a measured correctness trap: `gh api -f reason=x` builds a flat body the dispatch API does not read as an input, so the causal publish kick would start with an EMPTY reason, be indistinguishable from a keepalive kick, and get deduped away by the dashboard's freshness check — "the exact failure this whole change exists to remove". The fix is `-f 'inputs[reason]=metrics-publish'`. This PR is the first to make that step body executable, and it leaves the one branch carrying a documented, silently-reverting invariant on the unreachable side of a constant.
issues.fix_hint: Make it a keyword parameter — `def run_keepalive_leg(script, specs, *, metrics_result="failure", ...)` — and pass it through. Then add one row driving the metrics leg with `metrics_result="success"` that pins the dispatch argv by equality, including the literal `-f inputs[reason]=metrics-publish`, so a regression to `-f reason=` reds here.
issues.title: METRICS_RESULT is hardcoded to "failure" in the shared harness, so the metrics leg's causal publish branch stays unexecutable

issues.body: The THE ANCHOR block now reads `... and dispatch.yml is the one listed workflow where it does not: since the` / `# #819 tick` / `# floor, a within-floor ring concludes ...`. The inserted sentences pushed the original wrap without reflowing the tail, leaving `# #819 tick` alone on a line mid-sentence. Cosmetic only, but this block is load-bearing documentation that reviewers of this leg read first.
issues.fix_hint: Reflow the paragraph to the file's ~100-column comment width so `#819 tick floor` sits on one line.
issues.title: Comment rewrap left a two-word orphan line

verdict.summary:
The intent is right — #922's lesson (a run no longer implies the work) recurs as #1375's ingestion-rejection fingerprint, and that is a real defect worth closing. The tests are genuinely non-vacuous: the fresh-rejected-ahead-of-stale-accepted fixture flips red if the filter is inverted, the new `code = 64 if 'gh-stub: unexpected argv'` carry-out closes the hole where an unmodelled read looked like an empty stale anchor, and narrowing STUB_LIVE_FAIL to the live-filter branch correctly preserves the #559 fail-open rows now that both reads share `per_page=30`. Three problems block it.

(1) BLOCKER — the discriminator is dropped. ci-latency-alert.py:307-311 states that a scheduled run held by an ENVIRONMENT protection rule also concludes `action_required`, and that `jobs.total_count == 0` is the ONLY thing separating it from ingestion rejection. Every run-anchored target of this leg — metrics.yml, conflict-resolver.yml, curate.yml, groom-core.yml, and dashboard.yml for the metrics leg — gates on `dispatch-secrets`. The diff excludes all `action_required` runs with no job-count check, so a SETTLED approval-gated run (status `completed`, invisible to the #559 live guard) becomes "no accepted run" and the target is kicked every 15 minutes, each kick producing another gated run: the #559 storm class through a new door. The comment names the divergence but not the consequence, and no row covers it.

(2) MAJOR — on an empty anchor the unguarded `gh api -X POST` runs under `set -euo pipefail`. In the ingestion-rejection state this targets, that POST is the call most likely to fail, and a failure aborts the step, dropping every later spec. metrics.yml is first, so one rejected workflow wedges the keepalive for the other five. The stub's `*/dispatches) exit 0` hides it.

(3) MAJOR — the `::error::` text asserts one cause for three conditions (read failure via `|| true`, zero runs, approval-gated), and the anchor read cannot be made to fail in the harness at… [truncated 67 chars]
